To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
2, 2′-dipridyl and phenanthroline, two chelating agents, inhibit the hydroxylyation of proline, the synthesis of collagen, and the synthesis of noncollagenous proteins.

The action of chelators on collagen synthesis is not due to the inhibition of the incorporation of proline into collagenous and other proteins, but is due to the inhibition or the proline hydroxy-lase.

1) chelating agents inhibit the incorporation of [14C]-proline into collagen and noncollagenous proteins, 2) the inhibition of hydroxyproline synthesis is correlated with the stability constant of the ferrous chelate, 3) the inhibition of the synthesis of collagen is correlated with the concentration of the chelating agent and 4) the inhibition of collagen synthesis by chelating agents is due to the inhibition of the hydroxylation reaction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of the action of some chelates on proline hydroxylase and on the incorporation of proline into proteins.
the study of the mechanism of the action of 2,2'-dipyridyl (2,2'-Dipy) and 1, 10-phenanthrolin (Phen).
the mechanism of the action of some chelators on proline hydroxylase and the effect of chelators on collagen synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

2,9-DMP inhibits hydroxylation of Pro and incorporation of Pro into non-collagen proteins, but not into collagen proteins, and that 1,10-P inhibits hydroxylyation of Pro and incorporation into both collagen and non-collageneous proteins.
the action of 2,2’-dipyridine on collagen synthesis is a consequence of the inhibition of prolyl hydroxylase.
chelating agents act on the hydroxylation process and on the formation of collagen by inhibition of the ferroprotoporphyrin IX.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the action of chalating agents on the proline hydroxyation and the synthesis of noncollagenous proteins is not due to their action on the enzyme system but to the inhibition of the transport of proline into cells or into the site of hydroxylation.

the action of chalating agents on prolyl hydroxylase is a direct one and that it is not mediated by the inhibition of oxygen uptake by the cells or by the inhibition of the incorporation of amino acids into proteins.
chelation of iron in the tissue inhibits proline hydroxyation and the synthesis of both collagenous and noncollagenous proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the 3D model is a powerful tool for the design of novel and potent chelating agents.

the action of chela-ting agents on hydroxylation of collagen proline is a consequence of the inhibition of ferrous ion uptake by the cells, and not of the inhibition of the enzyme itself by a chelate.
chelating agents inhibit the incorporation of [14C]-proline into the collagenous proteins.
